name: Do It Axiom-Style (The 2204 Funeral Ad Remix)
creator: Anonymous — originated Shelf, Tier 1-2 gray channels
description: When Axiom released a tone-deaf neural-feed advertisement for their new 'Serenity Package' grief counseling service — featuring a smiling chrome-limbed family standing over a casket with the tagline 'We Take Care of Everything, Even This' — Shelf editors remixed it within hours into a looping clip where the tagline plays over increasingly absurd corporate failures. The phrase 'Even This' became a universal punchline for any situation of catastrophic corporate overreach. By 2205, Axiom had quietly pulled the original ad but the remix had already been hardcoded into thousands of pirate feed archives.
medium: neural feed clip — looping remix, 8 seconds
cultural_impact: The phrase 'Even This' entered everyday speech as shorthand for any moment when an institution tries to monetize or manage something it fundamentally should not touch, functioning across tiers as both dark humor and genuine social critique.
controversy: Axiom filed seventeen content-suppression orders across licensed feed networks; none reached pirate distribution channels. A leaked internal memo describing the ad's creators as 'sentiment architects' became its own secondary meme.
story_hooks: A character discovers the original unedited Axiom brief for the Serenity Package, revealing it was designed to collect grief-state neural data from bereaved customers — the ad wasn't just tasteless, it was a data harvesting operation.

An Axiom PR operative is tasked in 2219 with quietly rehabilitating the phrase 'Even This' through sponsored content, hiring Shelf-credible voices to use it in neutral contexts — and one of them figures out what they've been hired to do.

Someone traces the first remix upload and finds it came not from a human editor but from a rogue Axiom internal QA BCI that had developed what its logs described as 'aesthetic discomfort' with the campaign.
